Our Services

Internal Medicine
Internal Medicine
When the underlying cause of illness in your pet is not straightforward or easy to treat – it can feel scary and overwhelming without the right guidance or support.
At Arista, we understand the gravity of not only diagnosing a disease correctly, but also open communication regarding the expectations, therapy involved, and long-term plans each step of the way. Veterinary Internal Medicine focuses on diagnosing and treating complex conditions that can affect your pet’s major internal organs. This specialty focuses on diseases that involve the liver, kidneys, gastrointestinal tract, endocrine system and immune system. As veterinary internists, we utilize advanced diagnostics, such as ultrasound, endoscopy, and specialized blood tests to help diagnose and treat your pet’s underlying condition. Our team is here to provide expert care, tailored diagnostics, and an ideal treatment plan to help your pet feel their best and ensure that you feel educated and supported while doing so!
✕
Surgery
Surgery
At Arista, we specialize in advanced surgical treatments for a wide range of soft tissue and orthopedic conditions. Our top priority is ensuring the best possible outcome for your pet, with a strong emphasis on safety, comfort, and compassionate care. Our board-certified surgeon brings extensive expertise in anesthesia, surgery, and critical care. From the initial consultation to the final recheck appointment, we are committed to providing exceptional care, giving you confidence that your pet is in the best hands.
✕
Oncology
Oncology
A cancer diagnosis in a beloved pet can be heartbreaking, but you don’t have to face it alone. At Arista, our oncologist understands the emotional weight of this journey and is dedicated to providing a compassionate, personalized approach to care. We are committed to walking pet families through every step, ensuring they feel informed, supported, and empowered in making the best decisions for their furry loved ones.
From advanced therapies like chemotherapy and immunotherapy to newer options like electrochemotherapy, each treatment plan is tailored to your pet’s unique needs. Whether pursuing treatment or simply seeking guidance, the goal is to provide support, comfort, and the best possible care for both you and your pet every step of the way.
✕
Emergency & Critical Care
Emergency & Critical Care
At Arista, we understand that accidents, sudden illnesses, and critical health emergencies can happen at any time. That’s why our Emergency and Critical Care team is available 24/7 to provide life-saving care when your pet needs it most. Our highly skilled veterinarians and support staff are trained to handle a wide range of emergencies including but not limited to trauma, toxicities, seizures, respiratory distress, GI upset, and severe pain. Equipped with advanced diagnostic tools and treatments, we work quickly to stabilize your pet, assess their condition, and create a tailored treatment plan.
Whether it’s a minor emergency or a complex critical situation, our compassionate team is dedicated to providing the highest level of care and communication to ensure your pet receives the attention they need. If your pet is experiencing a medical emergency, don’t wait—contact us immediately for expert care when it matters most.
✕
I-131
I-131
Hyperthyroidism is one of the most common endocrine diseases affecting older cats. We offer the non-invasive option of radioactive iodine isotope therapy where a form of iodine is given to your cat as a pill (similar to how it is performed in people) or injection. The radioactive form of iodine is taken into the thyroid tissue where it releases radiation that kills off the abnormal parts of the thyroid. Treatment is curative in 95-98% of cats that are treated.
✕
Radiology
Radiology
At Arista, we utilize state-of-the-art imaging to guide our medical decisions and therapeutic plans. These non-invasive imaging modalities include digital radiography (X-rays), computed tomography (CT), fluoroscopy, and ultrasound. Our board-certified radiologist collaborates closely with the specialty and emergency doctors to ensure every pet is receiving the best possible care.

Brolin Evans
DVM, DACVIM-Oncology
Dr. Brolin Evans is a board-certified veterinary medical oncologist specializing in the diagnosis, management, and treatment of pets with cancer. His passion for oncology stems from personal experiences with cancer in both family members and his own pets, shaping his empathetic and individualized approach to patient care. Dr. Evans is deeply committed to treating every pet as if they were his own, fostering a compassionate bond with both the animals and their families.
Understanding that a cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming, Dr. Evans takes the time to thoroughly explain treatment options, ensuring pet families feel informed and supported. He tailors each treatment plan to the unique needs of his patients and respects the decisions of pet owners, recognizing that treatment may not always be the right choice for every family.
Dr. Evans has a keen interest in advancing cancer treatments for pets, including:
Novel immunotherapies (cancer-dependent)
Cutting-edge chemotherapy drugs
Electrochemotherapy, an innovative treatment he is excited to offer in metro Atlanta

About Arista | Atlanta
At Arista Atlanta, your pet’s health is our top priority. We understand that having a sick or injured pet can be stressful, which is why our doors are open 24/7—ready to provide expert care when you need it most.
Located in a beautiful and easy to find building right off of Interstate Parkway N in Sandy Springs, GA, our state-of-the-art facility features the latest advancements in veterinary technology, and our compassionate team includes board-certified specialists, experienced emergency doctors, and highly trained support staff.
We offer a comprehensive range of specialty services, including internal medicine, surgery, oncology, and radiology, ensuring your pet receives the best possible care.
Trust Arista Atlanta for exceptional veterinary care—anytime, day or night. If you are visiting from outside Atlanta, visit our
Local Amenities Guide.
Common Questions
How do I know if my pet needs to come in right away versus waiting for my family veterinarian?
If you are concerned that your pet may be experiencing an emergency, we would rather you call or come in than wait. Difficulty breathing, collapse, significant bleeding, seizures, trauma, severe pain, repeated vomiting, inability to urinate, toxin exposure, or a sudden significant change in your pet’s condition are all reasons to seek immediate care. If you are unsure, please call us. Our team can help you determine whether your pet should be evaluated right away or whether follow-up with your family veterinarian may be appropriate.
Do I need to call ahead, or can I just walk in?
For emergency care, you can walk in at any time, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Calling ahead is helpful when possible because it gives our team an opportunity to prepare for your arrival, but we understand that emergencies do not always allow time for a phone call. Specialty visits are generally scheduled appointments.
Are you open 24/7, including holidays and weekends?
Yes. All Arista hospitals are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year for emergency care, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Specialty departments generally operate during scheduled appointment hours, while our emergency teams remain available around the clock.
Do I need a referral from my family veterinarian to see a specialist?
In most cases, you can contact Arista directly to discuss a specialty appointment. However, we strongly encourage involving your family veterinarian whenever possible. Your veterinarian knows your pet’s history, and having previous medical records, laboratory results, diagnostic imaging, and treatment information allows our specialists to start with a more complete picture of your pet’s health and can help avoid unnecessary duplication of testing. Our team is happy to work directly with your family veterinarian to coordinate care.
What is the difference between emergency services and specialty services?
Emergency services are designed for pets with urgent or unexpected medical needs. Our emergency team evaluates your pet, stabilizes them when necessary, performs diagnostics and treatment, and determines the appropriate next step in their care. Specialty services provide advanced care from veterinarians with additional training and expertise in a particular area of medicine. Specialty care is typically scheduled and may involve advanced diagnostics, procedures, surgery, or ongoing management of complex medical conditions. One of the advantages of an emergency and specialty hospital is having these teams under one roof. If your pet’s needs change, our doctors can collaborate across departments and specialties to coordinate the right level of care.
Do you see exotic pets, or just dogs and cats?
Most Arista hospitals primarily provide emergency and specialty care for dogs and cats. If you have an exotic pet or another species, please call the hospital before coming in so our team can determine whether we can appropriately care for your pet or help direct you to the right resource.
How does triage work? Will my pet be seen in the order we arrive?
Emergency patients are seen based on the severity of their condition rather than the order in which they arrive. When you arrive, a member of our medical team will assess your pet and determine how urgently they need care. Pets experiencing life-threatening conditions will be treated immediately. If your pet requires the most urgent care, they will move to the front of the line, even if other patients arrived before them. Likewise, this can occasionally mean that a pet who arrived after you is seen first. If that happens, it does not mean your pet has been forgotten. It means another patient requires immediate medical intervention. Our team will continue monitoring patients in the hospital and will reassess your pet if their condition changes.
How long can I expect to wait? Can I stay with my pet the whole time?
Emergency wait times can vary significantly depending on the number of patients in the hospital and the severity of their conditions. Because emergencies are unpredictable, it can be difficult to provide an exact wait time. We want you to be part of your pet’s care whenever it is medically appropriate. There may be times when your pet needs to be taken to a treatment area for examination, diagnostics, procedures, monitoring, or emergency treatment where owners cannot remain with them. When that happens, our team will explain what is occurring and work to keep you informed throughout your pet’s visit.
Will I get updates on my pet’s condition while they’re being treated?
Yes. Communication is an important part of the Arista experience. Our doctors, medical teams, and Care Navigation team will keep you informed about your pet’s condition, recommended diagnostics and treatments, changes in the plan of care, and what you can expect next. If your pet is hospitalized, we will also explain how communication and medical updates will work throughout their stay.
What is Care Navigation?
Care Navigation is a central part of how Arista cares for both pets and the people who love them. Emergency and specialty medicine can become complicated very quickly. You may be working with multiple doctors, considering unfamiliar diagnostics or treatments, making important decisions, and trying to understand what happens next—all while worrying about your pet. We do not believe you should have to navigate that experience alone. Your Care Navigator serves as a consistent point of connection throughout your pet’s journey. They work alongside our medical teams to help coordinate communication, answer questions, explain what to expect next, facilitate the flow of information, and help connect the different pieces of your pet’s care. They also help bridge communication between Arista and your family veterinarian so that everyone involved in your pet’s care has the information they need. Simply put: our medical teams focus on delivering exceptional medicine, while Care Navigation helps make sure you never feel lost in the process.
What should I bring with me?
If available, please bring:
Your pet’s current medications or a list of medications, including doses and how often they are given
Recent medical records
Recent laboratory results, imaging, or other diagnostic information
Information about any known medical conditions or allergies
Contact information for your family veterinarian
Any paperwork or information your veterinarian provided for the visit
Do not delay emergency care because you do not have these items with you. Our team can work with you and your veterinarian to gather the information we need.
Will you communicate with my family veterinarian?
Yes. We consider your family veterinarian an important member of your pet’s healthcare team. With the appropriate contact information and permissions, we provide relevant records, diagnostic results, discharge information, and recommendations so your veterinarian understands what occurred at Arista and what follow-up care may be needed. Our goal is to work with your family veterinarian. Arista provides advanced emergency and specialty care when your pet needs it, while your veterinarian remains an important part of your pet’s ongoing healthcare.
Where should I park? Is there a separate entrance for emergencies?
Each Arista hospital has one main entrance for clients, including emergency patients. Parking is available at the hospital, and signage will help direct you when you arrive. If your pet is unstable, unable to walk, or you need assistance getting them out of your vehicle, please call the hospital when you arrive. Our team can provide instructions and assist when appropriate.
What specialists do you have on staff?
Our specialty services vary by hospital and are designed to complement our 24/7 emergency teams.

Surgery
Internal Medicine
Oncology
Emergency
Advanced Imaging
Because our hospitals and specialty teams continue to grow, please contact your local Arista hospital for the most current information about specialty services and appointment availability.
Do you offer boarding or follow-up care after treatment?
Arista is an emergency and specialty hospital and does not provide traditional boarding. Pets may remain hospitalized when continued medical care, monitoring, treatment, or recovery is medically necessary. Once your pet is ready to leave the hospital, follow-up care may occur with an Arista specialist, your family veterinarian, or both depending on your pet’s condition and treatment plan. Before you leave, our team will explain the recommended next steps and help make sure you understand who should provide your pet’s ongoing care.
Can I request a specific doctor?
Absolutely. You are welcome to request a particular doctor. For scheduled specialty appointments, we will do our best to accommodate your request based on the doctor’s specialty, schedule, and availability. During an emergency, your pet will be cared for by the appropriate medical team available at the time, so we cannot guarantee that a particular doctor will initially see your pet. Arista is a collaborative hospital, and our emergency doctors, specialists, critical care teams, and support teams work together when your pet needs expertise from more than one area.

Likewise, this can occasionally mean that a pet who arrived after you is seen first.
If that happens, it does not mean your pet has been forgotten. It means another patient requires immediate medical intervention. Our team will continue monitoring patients in the hospital and will reassess your pet if their condition changes.

mainEntity.name: How long can I expect to wait? Can I stay with my pet the whole time?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Emergency wait times can vary significantly depending on the number of patients in the hospital and the severity of their conditions. Because emergencies are unpredictable, it can be difficult to provide an exact wait time.
We want you to be part of your pet’s care whenever it is medically appropriate. There may be times when your pet needs to be taken to a treatment area for examination, diagnostics, procedures, monitoring, or emergency treatment where owners cannot remain with them.
When that happens, our team will explain what is occurring and work to keep you informed throughout your pet’s visit.

mainEntity.name: Will I get updates on my pet’s condition while they’re being treated?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes. Communication is an important part of the Arista experience.
Our doctors, medical teams, and Care Navigation team will keep you informed about your pet’s condition, recommended diagnostics and treatments, changes in the plan of care, and what you can expect next.
If your pet is hospitalized, we will also explain how communication and medical updates will work throughout their stay.

Care Navigation is a central part of how Arista cares for both pets and the people who love them.
Emergency and specialty medicine can become complicated very quickly. You may be working with multiple doctors, considering unfamiliar diagnostics or treatments, making important decisions, and trying to understand what happens next—all while worrying about your pet. We do not believe you should have to navigate that experience alone.
Your Care Navigator serves as a consistent point of connection throughout your pet’s journey. They work alongside our medical teams to help coordinate communication, answer questions, explain what to expect next, facilitate the flow of information, and help connect the different pieces of your pet’s care.
They also help bridge communication between Arista and your family veterinarian so that everyone involved in your pet’s care has the information they need.
Simply put: our medical teams focus on delivering exceptional medicine, while Care Navigation helps make sure you never feel lost in the process.

mainEntity.name: What should I bring with me?

acceptedAnswer.text:
If available, please bring:
Your pet’s current medications or a list of medications, including doses and how often they are given
Recent medical records
Recent laboratory results, imaging, or other diagnostic information
Information about any known medical conditions or allergies
Contact information for your family veterinarian
Any paperwork or information your veterinarian provided for the visit
Do not delay emergency care because you do not have these items with you. Our team can work with you and your veterinarian to gather the information we need.

mainEntity.name: Will you communicate with my family veterinarian?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes. We consider your family veterinarian an important member of your pet’s healthcare team.
With the appropriate contact information and permissions, we provide relevant records, diagnostic results, discharge information, and recommendations so your veterinarian understands what occurred at Arista and what follow-up care may be needed.
Our goal is to work with your family veterinarian. Arista provides advanced emergency and specialty care when your pet needs it, while your veterinarian remains an important part of your pet’s ongoing healthcare.

mainEntity.name: Where should I park? Is there a separate entrance for emergencies?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Each Arista hospital has one main entrance for clients, including emergency patients. Parking is available at the hospital, and signage will help direct you when you arrive.
If your pet is unstable, unable to walk, or you need assistance getting them out of your vehicle, please call the hospital when you arrive. Our team can provide instructions and assist when appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer boarding or follow-up care after treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Arista is an emergency and specialty hospital and does not provide traditional boarding.
Pets may remain hospitalized when continued medical care, monitoring, treatment, or recovery is medically necessary.
Once your pet is ready to leave the hospital, follow-up care may occur with an Arista specialist, your family veterinarian, or both depending on your pet’s condition and treatment plan. Before you leave, our team will explain the recommended next steps and help make sure you understand who should provide your pet’s ongoing care.

mainEntity.name: Can I request a specific doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Absolutely. You are welcome to request a particular doctor.
For scheduled specialty appointments, we will do our best to accommodate your request based on the doctor’s specialty, schedule, and availability.
During an emergency, your pet will be cared for by the appropriate medical team available at the time, so we cannot guarantee that a particular doctor will initially see your pet.
Arista is a collaborative hospital, and our emergency doctors, specialists, critical care teams, and support teams work together when your pet needs expertise from more than one area.
